titleEn: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
headline: Şeffaf Kafalı Tuhaf Derin Deniz Balığı Çarpıcı 4K'da Görüntülendi.
details: Deep-sea researchers have captured stunning new footage of an extraordinarily rare fish with a transparent head and rotating eyes nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface.
brief: A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures.
summary: A rare encounter nearly 2,000 feet beneath the ocean's surface gave scientists an extraordinary opportunity to film one of the deep sea's most unusual creatures. Researchers from the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) spotted a barreleye fish ( Macropinna microstoma ), a mysterious species known for its transparent head and remarkable eyes that can rotate to track prey. The discovery occurred during an expedition aboard the research vessel David Packard . It marked only the eleventh time MBARI scientists have encountered this elusive fish during nearly four decades of ocean exploration.
